chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Neal Hefti as trumpeter and arranger
summary: Hefti joined as a trumpeter in 1942, began writing for the band, and returned off and on; Barnet remains a friend.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And how long did -- did Neal -- you said that Neal wrote for you then too, didn't you?

Well, Neal joined my band as a trumpet player at first, in 1942. And of course he started writing for me then, and he would up with Woody too. But then he was back off and on, different times, playing and arranging before he got into his own thing. And we remain to this day very dear friends. In fact I just spoke to him the day before yesterday.
I know Leonard said he was coming back, but I -- I wrote to him when Frances died and I haven't heard from him. I didn't know, wasn't sure he was back.
Yeah, he just bought a home in Toluca Lake.
No. No. He's going to live there with his son. And I said, 'How are you doing, Neal?' He said, 'I've got ups and downs, but it's getting better.'
